A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BOPE-MoNNE research. The 22-page v1 and 26-page v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures that can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization benchmarks, component ablations, noise experiments, and neural-network uncertainty investigations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds benchmark results, comparison methods, acquisition-function tests, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The monotonic ensemble, hinge loss including tied preferences, output normalization, qNEIUU, and independent EUBO are retained. Algorithm 1 is relocated and its loop indexing corrected. Newly documented initialization and optimizer details do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 adds ZDT1 with a 10-dimensional input, two objectives, and LinearExponential utility to the five existing BOPE benchmarks. The earlier synthetic utility-fitting and vanilla-BO studies remain. Bradley-Terry noise is discussed but is not used in additional BOPE experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds BOPE-Linear, a positive-coefficient linear utility model using Laplace approximation. Figure 20 additionally compares EUBO-equipped MoNNE against IEUBO-equipped MoNNE. The existing main baselines and the comparators in the observed-versus-arbitrary-output experiment are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a comparison using two objective evaluations per preference query, whereas the main experiment retains one evaluation per query (Appendix A.5.3, Figure 12). Noise testing adds sigma = 0.5 to the existing 0 and 0.1 settings. The main initialization sample counts and regret metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the diagnostic evidence: Figure 20 directly tests IEUBO against EUBO with and without noise; Figure 12 examines the PBO evaluation-budget issue; Figure 14 adds optimization trajectories; and Figure 22 extends noise robustness testing. Existing component, activation, depth, and HMC analyses are retained, with several benchmark analyses extended to ZDT1.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 repetitions and mean plus/minus one standard error for BOPE plots, 10 repetitions for vanilla BO, and 50 repetitions for the surrogate-assessment procedure. Additional results retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practices; no new significance tests or confidence-interval procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for ZDT1, BOPE-Linear, acquisition comparisons, evaluation-budget controls, and stronger noise. For example, ZDT1 prediction accuracies are 0.92, 0.96, and 0.94 for GP, MoNNE, and BMNN (Table 2). New findings include BOPE-Linear's advantage on the linear-utility benchmark and EUBO's competitiveness without noise. The five retained benchmark rows in Tables 1–3 keep their values.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5.1 newly defines a scaled Bradley-Terry choice model and mathematically compares its probabilities with Gaussian utility noise, including their limiting behavior. The monotonic approximation theorem and the expected-maximum derivation underlying IEUBO are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the principal claims: monotonic ensembles improve BOPE, handle noisy preferences, and offer an alternative to HMC-trained BNNs for pairwise learning. The expanded description of uncertainty methods does not introduce a new contribution absent from v1.

C2.justification: v2 links IEUBO's benefit more specifically to potentially incorrect correlations learned under noise and acknowledges EUBO's competitiveness without noise. It adds the linear-model applicability qualification and Bradley-Terry/Gaussian interpretation, expands the PBO comparability discussion, and revises the noise discussion around the stronger-noise results.

D1.justification: v1 promises code after acceptance; v2 supplies a repository URL. v2 also documents weight and bias initialization, Adam's learning rate, cosine-scheduler parameters, and stopping training when hinge loss reaches zero. These substantially improve reproducibility information, without establishing that the earlier experiments used different settings.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands PBO coverage with projective, multi-objective, amortized, theoretical, and abstract-property work. It clarifies the distinction between comparisons of designs and comparisons of objective outputs, and reframes Ozaki et al. as offering monotonicity with reduced flexibility. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained. v2 revises selected explanations, replaces the inaccurate non-parametric characterization of neural networks, folds the ablation section into Experimental Results, and reorganizes appendix settings. The title and author information are edited, and acknowledgments replace the generic impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Algorithm 1 and Tables 1–2 move to the appendix, benchmark plots are rearranged into six-problem displays with revised legends, and new noise-model, budget-control, trajectory, and acquisition-comparison figures are added. Many underlying explanatory graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added linear baseline, acquisition and budget controls, and stronger-noise tests make the existing claims easier to assess. Training details and code-access information improve reproducibility. These are incremental gains over v1's already substantial experiments. Some broad superiority wording remains insufficiently qualified, particularly Figure 3's caption despite the newly reported linear-baseline exception.
